title: Quarterly Roaming Ledger for Private Deploy Activation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Create a compact, actionable quarterly roadmap artifact (the 'Roaming Ledger') that sequences activation waves, capacity hedges, and OKR-aligned experiments for Private/VPC/on-prem enterprise features. The ledger is intended for cross-functional stakeholders (product, eng, infra, sales, solutions) to reduce coordination friction during rollouts and provide a single source of truth for tranche activation decisions.

Scope: enrollment/activation cohorts, gating criteria, compatibility matrix, capacity runway, canary windows, support runbook readiness, and metrics mapped to OKRs. Exclusions: deep technical runbooks and per-customer SOPs which remain in the private-deploy runbook repo.
objectives: Define 3 activation cohorts (Pilot, Lighthouse, General) with explicit acceptance criteria
Map every cohort to capacity/reservation lanes and failure budget thresholds
Align deliverables to two OKRs: 1) Reliable private activation (SLA attainment) 2) Activation throughput (tenants/day)
Produce a decision ledger and escalation matrix for mid-rollout compatibility regressions
success_metrics: Pilot cohort: 3 lighthouse customers onboarded within 30 days
SLA success: 99.5% baseline latencies for dedicated routes within 72 hours of activation
Activation throughput: average 0.8 tenants/day in pilot-to-lighthouse phase
Rollback rate: <5% of activations require a rollback intervention
milestones: M1: Ledger draft and stakeholder review (2026-03-08)
M2: Engineering compatibility verification and perf bench (2026-03-22)
M3: Security & legal sign-off for cohort gating (2026-04-01)
M5: Post-pilot retrospective and acceptance decision (2026-05-05)
acceptance_criteria: Ledger accepted by PM, Eng lead, and Security (signoff in Confluence)
All cohort gating tests green in staging cluster for 14 consecutive runs
Observability dashboards instrumented with tenant-level latency/cost signals
Oncall and support runbooks published and practiced in a tabletop exercise
risks: Kernel/quantization mismatch causes performance regressions for onprem variants
Capacity contention across dedicated pools if autoscaling thresholds are misaligned
Legal/compliance delays for region-specific data residency requirements
Customer integration variance (homegrown proxies) increases support overhead
decisions: Use tranche-based activation rather than full fleet rollouts to limit blast radius
Default routing for pilot tenants will be to dedicated capacity lane A with fallback to hosted API B
Require KMS integration for any tenant with regulated data prior to activation
